# Rules

Every rule below runs on every plate unless a job turns it off.

A rule reports what it measured and what the limit was. It never changes
anything: a plate that fails a rule comes out of the compiler exactly as
it was asked for, with the failure written down beside it.

| rule | severity | what it checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `legend-missing-glyph` | error | the face cannot draw something the legend asks for |
| `legend-overrun` | error | the legend is wider than the engraving area even after fitting |
| `engraving-inside-area` | error | every mark has to be inside the engraving area |
| `feature-clearance` | error | engraving has to keep its distance from holes and cutouts |
| `feature-on-plate` | error | a hole or cutout that is not on the plate it belongs to |
| `border-on-plate` | error | the border groove has to be on the plate with room to spare |
| `border-clearance` | warning | the legend has to stay off the engraved border |
| `stroke-merge` | error | two strokes come closer than the groove they cut, so they run together |
| `stroke-self-merge` | error | a stroke comes back on itself closer than the groove it cuts |
| `stroke-stub` | warning | a stroke too short to be anything but a dimple |
| `letter-weight` | warning | the groove is too wide for the size of the lettering |
| `depth-window` | error | the depth has to be one the stock will take |
| `cutter-reach` | error | the cutter has to reach the depth asked for |
| `pass-count` | warning | a cut that needs a lot of passes is worth a second look |
| `parallel-cutter-buried` | warning | a parallel cutter taken deeper than it is wide |
| `odd-lettering-height` | note | a lettering height that is not one the shop sets up for |

## Severity

`error` stops a job. `warning` is printed and the job goes on, because
the operator is the one who decides whether heavy lettering matters on
this plate. `note` is something worth knowing and nothing more.

## The numbers

| number | value | what it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| joint fraction | 0.02 | of the cap height, within which two strokes are joined |
| fold ratio | 1.5 | times further along a stroke than across it before it is a fold |
| weight ratio | 0.25 | of the cap height, past which the groove is too wide |
| sensible passes | 6 | passes, past which the depth is worth a second look |
| plunge ratio | 1 | times its own width, past which a parallel cutter is buried |
